touches.text: Prebuild face: the chart chain, eight machines, each answering one question before a build begins: orient (what is asked, where does it live), constrain (what bounds it), survey (what already exists), decompose (how does it split), triage (what first, by what standard), hypothesize (what do we expect, how would we know we're wrong), validate (what does DONE mean, measured), and after the build, verdict (what done actually meant).

Each stage moves from the model to deterministic code once a proof a hollow build could not pass can hold it; hypothesize stays with the model longest. Validate sends a local miss back to hypothesize and a structural one back to design. A build that finds new work spawns children that enter at decompose.
The chart chain machines (9.3.2): orient, constrain, survey, decompose, triage, hypothesize, validate, verdict.

The verdict's instrument run is a seal-grade run, so it runs where the sealer runs (9.4.2.3.3.1), under bubblewrap. A box without bubblewrap (Windows) asks for it and does not run it itself. A bwrap-only tooth reads not-run on such a box, never red; its outcome is the sealer's. - CC
Entry gates exist only to kick back what doesn't meet the entry requirements. Nothing in them is about who writes what.

The inspectors are not assumed correct; they are examined when they refuse. After a gate refuses, an LLM sets the refusing sieve's intention and why beside the ticket's intention and why and asks: is this sieve the best we can do right now? If yes, the ticket changes. If no, the sieve is fixed through its own ticket and proof. Either way the system improves. WHY: a disagreement becomes an update to an intention or its implementation, never a conversation about procedure. The sieves stay deterministic and never weigh a why; the LLM check comes only after a failure, and it is never a lock pick because it has no third outcome. Nothing passes a ticket over a red.
A sieve's rule follows the ticket's kind, read off the ticket, so it stays deterministic; 17.11.6 is left for what the rules do not cover.

conflicts.ticket_says: validate door refuses a criterion whose instrument does not extract to a command this box can start; extract_command returns None for path heads not executable on THIS box, so no runner calls
conflicts.why: Outline describes: 'A box without bubblewrap (Windows) asks for it and does not run it itself. A bwrap-only tooth reads not-run on such a box, never red.' This prescribes that Windows can draft and proceed with instruments it cannot run locally (delegating to the sealer). The ticket's logic refuses non-executable paths at validate time on the box where validate runs. If validate runs on Windows and checks os.access(X_OK) on Windows, instruments like 'bubblewrap /path' (or the POSIX test path in the ticket example) would be refused, preventing Windows from drafting them. This contradicts the outline's description of Windows asking for such instruments.
